sentence: The skull is formed by 22 bones in two groups, the brain case and the face.
note: OpenStax: skull formed by 22 bones, eight in the brain case and 14 facial. StatPearls: 22 bones in two regions.

sentence: The brain case houses and shields the brain, while the facial bones give the face its structure and form the upper and lower jaws.
note: OpenStax: brain case houses and shields the brain; facial bones give the face its structure and form upper and lower jaws.

sentence: Only the mandible, or lower jaw, is movable; the other bones are held together by immobile fibrous joints called sutures.
note: OpenStax: mandible is the only moveable skull bone; suture defined as an immobile fibrous joint connecting skull bones other than the mandible.

sentence: The 3D model shows each bone separately and also includes the hyoid bone, which is not part of the skull.
note: First clause describes the site atlas (Hyoid bone is an atlas structure). OpenStax: hyoid contacts no other bone, so not part of skull.

sentence: Twenty-two: eight in the brain case and fourteen in the face
note: OpenStax: 22 skull bones; brain case eight bones; facial bones 14 (six paired types, two single).

sentence: Paired parietal and temporal bones; single frontal, occipital, sphenoid and ethmoid bones
note: OpenStax: brain case formed by paired parietal and temporal bones plus unpaired frontal, occipital, sphenoid and ethmoid.

sentence: Paired maxilla, palatine, zygomatic, nasal, lacrimal and inferior nasal concha; single vomer and mandible
note: OpenStax: paired maxilla, palatine, zygomatic, nasal, lacrimal, inferior nasal conchae; unpaired vomer and mandible.

sentence: The mandible, the only movable bone of the skull, which meets the temporal bone at the temporomandibular joint
note: OpenStax: mandible only moveable skull bone; its condyle meets the mandibular fossa and articular tubercle of the temporal bone.

sentence: Coronal, sagittal, lambdoid and squamous
note: OpenStax skull section describes the coronal, sagittal, lambdoid and squamous sutures.

sentence: Anterior, middle and posterior cranial fossae; the foramen magnum lies in the posterior fossa
note: OpenStax: cranial cavity floor has three fossae deepening front to back; foramen magnum is a large opening in the posterior fossa.

sentence: CT scan for a severe head injury; plain skull X-rays are no longer carried out
note: NHS inform: CT scan judges seriousness and shows bleeding, bruising or swelling; skull X-rays no longer carried out.

sentence: The skull has two regions: the neurocranium, or brain case, which houses the brain, and the viscerocranium, which forms the face.
note: StatPearls: 22 bones in two regions, neurocranium houses the brain and viscerocranium forms the face. OpenStax: brain case houses the brain.

sentence: The brain case is made up of eight bones: the paired parietal and temporal bones and the single frontal, occipital, sphenoid and ethmoid bones.
note: OpenStax: brain case formed by eight bones, paired parietal and temporal plus unpaired frontal, occipital, sphenoid and ethmoid.

sentence: The face has fourteen bones: the paired maxilla, palatine, zygomatic, nasal and lacrimal bones and inferior nasal conchae, and the single vomer and mandible.
note: OpenStax: 14 facial bones, six paired (maxilla, palatine, zygomatic, nasal, lacrimal, inferior nasal conchae) and two unpaired (vomer, mandible).

sentence: The ethmoid is counted among the cranial bones but also contributes to the structures of the face.
note: OpenStax: ethmoid contributes to facial structures though it is counted among the cranial bones.

sentence: The hyoid bone is an independent bone that does not contact any other bone, so it is not counted as part of the skull.
note: OpenStax: hyoid is an independent bone that does not contact any other bone and thus is not part of the skull.

sentence: Sutures are fibrous joints in which connective tissue binds adjacent skull bones together.
note: OpenStax key terms: a suture is a junction where adjacent skull bones are united by fibrous connective tissue; 9.2 covers fibrous joints.

sentence: The coronal suture runs from side to side across the skull and joins the frontal bone to the right and left parietal bones.
note: OpenStax: coronal suture runs side to side across the skull and joins the frontal bone to the right and left parietal bones.

sentence: The sagittal suture runs along the midline of the skull, where the two parietal bones meet, and ends at the lambdoid suture.
note: OpenStax: sagittal suture runs down the midline of the top of the skull where parietal bones meet; ends by meeting the lambdoid suture.

sentence: The lambdoid suture lies at the back of the skull, where the occipital bone meets the parietal bones.
note: OpenStax: lambdoid suture sits at the back of the skull where the occipital bone meets the parietal (and temporal) bones.

sentence: The squamous suture, on the side of the skull, joins the squamous part of the temporal bone to the parietal bone.
note: OpenStax: squamous suture on the side of the skull links the squamous portion of the temporal bone to the parietal bone.

sentence: Skull sutures are classed as synarthroses, although a few may allow slight movement between cranial bones.
note: OpenStax 9.2: skull sutures classed functionally as synarthroses, though a few may allow minor shifting between cranial bones.

sentence: The mandible, or lower jaw, is the only movable bone of the skull.
note: OpenStax: mandible forms the lower jaw and is the only moveable bone of the skull.

sentence: Each side has a horizontal body and a vertical ramus, and the outer margin where they join is the angle.
note: OpenStax: each side has a horizontal body and a vertical ramus; the outside margin where they come together is the angle.

sentence: The flattened coronoid process on the ramus gives attachment to one of the biting muscles, while the condylar process is topped by the oval condyle.
note: OpenStax: flattened coronoid process gives attachment to a biting muscle; posterior condylar process is topped by the oval condyle.

sentence: The condyle meets the mandibular fossa and articular tubercle of the temporal bone at the temporomandibular joint, where an articular disc lies between the bones.
note: OpenStax 9.6: mandibular condyle meets the mandibular fossa and articular tubercle of the temporal bone; an articular disc sits between the bones.

sentence: Gliding and hinge movements at this joint lower and raise the jaw, move it forwards and backwards, and shift it from side to side.
note: OpenStax 9.6: gliding and hinge motions of the condyle produce elevation and depression, protraction and retraction, and lateral movements.

sentence: A major chewing muscle that raises the mandible arises from the zygomatic arch, which is formed by the zygomatic and temporal bones.
note: OpenStax: zygomatic arch has a part from the zygomatic bone and a part from the temporal bone; a major jaw-raising chewing muscle arises from it.

sentence: The floor of the cranial cavity forms three fossae that become deeper from front to back.
note: OpenStax 7.2: floor of the cranial cavity is described as three fossae that deepen from front to back.

sentence: The anterior fossa is the shallowest, and the lesser wings of the sphenoid form its back boundary.
note: OpenStax: anterior fossa is shallowest and most anterior; lesser wings of the sphenoid form its posterior boundary.

sentence: The middle fossa lies behind it, and its floor holds the optic canal, superior orbital fissure, foramen rotundum, foramen ovale and foramen spinosum.
note: OpenStax: middle fossa sits behind the anterior fossa; floor has optic canal, superior orbital fissure, foramina rotundum, ovale and spinosum.

sentence: The posterior fossa is the deepest, extending to the occipital bone, and contains the foramen magnum, internal acoustic meatus, jugular foramina and hypoglossal canals.
note: OpenStax: posterior fossa is deepest, from petrous ridge to occipital bone; lists foramen magnum, internal acoustic meatus, jugular foramina, hypoglossal canals.

sentence: The skull base has many openings that pass nerves and blood vessels.
note: StatPearls: the skull base sits beneath the brain and contains many openings that pass neural and vascular structures.

sentence: The foramen magnum, the largest, is the passage by which the brain connects with the spinal cord, and the vertebral arteries also pass through it.
note: StatPearls (via search summary): foramen magnum is the largest skull opening, connecting brain to spinal cord; vertebral arteries also pass through.

sentence: The optic canal transmits the optic nerve and the ophthalmic artery.
note: StatPearls (via search summary): optic canal transmits the optic nerve, ophthalmic artery, meningeal sheaths and sympathetic fibres.

sentence: Seven bones contribute to the walls of each orbit, which houses the eyeball and its muscles: the frontal, zygomatic, maxillary, palatine, ethmoid, lacrimal and sphenoid bones.
note: OpenStax: orbit walls formed by seven bones (frontal, zygomatic, maxillary, palatine, ethmoid, lacrimal, sphenoid); orbits house eyeballs and associated muscles.

sentence: The nasal septum divides the nasal cavity into halves; its upper part is the perpendicular plate of the ethmoid bone, its lower part is the vomer, and septal cartilage forms the front.
note: OpenStax: nasal septum divides the nasal cavity in halves; perpendicular plate of ethmoid above, vomer below, septal cartilage forms the anterior septum.

sentence: The sinuses sit within several skull bones: the frontal sinus, above the eyebrows, is the most anterior; the maxillary sinuses, below the orbits, are the largest; and the sphenoid sinus, within the sphenoid body, is the most posterior.
note: OpenStax: frontal sinus above eyebrows, most anterior; maxillary sinuses largest, below orbits; sphenoid sinus within sphenoid body, most posterior.

sentence: The ethmoid bone contains the ethmoid air cells, small air spaces between the orbit and the upper nasal cavity.
note: OpenStax: ethmoid holds ethmoid air cells; glossary defines them as small air spaces lying between the orbit and the upper nasal cavity.

sentence: At birth the skull bones are not yet fused.
note: OpenStax 7.5: fontanelles are the gaps between the not-yet-fused skull bones at birth.

sentence: The wide connective-tissue gaps between them, the fontanelles or soft spots, give the skull flexibility during birth, letting the bones move closer together or overlap slightly as the head passes through the birth canal.
note: OpenStax: fontanelles are soft spots; during birth they give the skull flexibility, bones moving closer or slightly overlapping in the birth canal.

sentence: After birth they allow the skull to keep growing as the brain enlarges, and they decrease in size and close in early childhood.
note: OpenStax 7.5: after birth fontanelles allow continued skull growth as brain enlarges; they decrease in size and disappear by age 2 (age omitted here).

sentence: The cranial vault forms by intramembranous ossification, in which embryonic mesenchyme turns directly into bone, whereas the skull base forms by endochondral ossification.
note: StatPearls: vault by intramembranous ossification, skull base by endochondral. OpenStax 7.5: embryonic mesenchyme converts directly into bone.

sentence: Late in life the sagittal, coronal and lambdoid sutures begin to ossify and fuse, a change called synostosis, meaning joined by bone.
note: OpenStax 9.2: connective tissue at some sutures ossifies, fusing bones (synostosis, joined by bone); late in life sagittal, coronal, lambdoid sutures begin to fuse.

sentence: Most skull fractures heal by themselves, particularly simple linear fractures, although healing can take many months.
note: NHS inform: most skull fractures heal by themselves, particularly simple linear fractures; healing can take many months.

sentence: At the pterion, where the frontal, parietal, temporal and sphenoid bones meet just above the ear, a blow to the side of the skull can tear the middle meningeal artery, a branch of the maxillary artery, and cause an epidural haematoma.
note: StatPearls skull entry: pterion joins frontal, parietal, temporal, sphenoid just above the pinna; blunt lateral trauma can injure the middle meningeal artery, causing epidural haematoma.

sentence: Arterial bleeding into the epidural space accumulates quickly and does not cross suture lines.
note: StatPearls skull entry: arterial haemorrhage in the epidural space accumulates quickly and does not cross suture lines.

sentence: Temporomandibular joint disorder is a painful condition that can arise from arthritis, cartilage wear, muscle strain from overuse or teeth grinding, disc damage or a jaw injury.
note: OpenStax 9.6: TMJ disorder is a painful condition with causes including arthritis, cartilage wear, muscle strain from overuse or teeth grinding, disc damage, jaw injury.

sentence: The NHS describes clicking, popping or grinding noises when the jaw moves as one of its features.
note: NHS temporomandibular disorder page (via search summary): clicking, popping or grinding noises when moving the jaw listed as a symptom.

where: section:Head injuries and how they are assessed
sentence: Most head injuries are not serious, but NHS advice lists signs that need urgent medical help, including a dent in the head, a head wound with something inside it, and fluid leaking from the ears or nose.
note: NHS head injury page (search summary): most head injuries not serious; urgent signs include a dent, wound with something inside, fluid from ears or nose.

where: section:Head injuries and how they are assessed
sentence: In hospital, a CT scan is used to judge how serious a severe head injury is, because it shows whether there is any bleeding, bruising or swelling in the brain.
note: NHS inform: CT scan is used to judge how serious the injury is and shows any bleeding, bruising or swelling in the brain.

where: section:Head injuries and how they are assessed
sentence: Plain skull X-rays are no longer carried out for this purpose, because they give little information about brain damage.
note: NHS inform: skull X-rays are no longer carried out as they do not provide information on brain damage.
